newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Queensland Cotton to build new ginnery.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Queensland Cotton to build new ginnery.

text.p: Queensland Cotton Holdings Ltd said on Friday it would construct a four-stand cotton ginnery at Dirranbandi in southwest Queensland.
With a capacity of 100,000 500-pound bales per season, the gin would be operational for the 1998 cotton season, it said.
Chief executive Richard Haire said that cotton production in the Dirranbandi area had grown, making construction of a gin feasible.
The region was expected to produce about 75,000 bales of cotton in 1998. If prices and weather conditions remained favourable, production was predicted to grow to 120,000 bales in 2002, he said.
Growers in the region currently had to bear substantial transport costs to gin their cotton elsewhere, he said.
The new gin would also allow the company to process any overflow from other areas, he said.
The company had already secured ginning commitments from growers in the region, he said.
Dirranbandi would be the company's eighth gin and would take its total ginning capacity to more than 680,000 bales.

Expansion of the ginning division followed a $2.5 million upgrade of module storage pads at Cecil Plains and Dalby, the construction of a 10,000 tonne capacity seed shed at Dalby and a $4.0 million extension to its Dalby ginning facility, he said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
